main_text.p: fragii tabulam Demosthenes in actione contra Lacritum nobis confervavit, maxime est conspicuum. Periculum vero potissimum iis, qui pecuniam mutuo dabant, hinc existebat, quod omnibus hujus generis contractibus hæs conditio cohæreret, si forte naufragio res cum nave perire contingeret, ne pecuniam repetere, multo minus usuram aut fœnus ex eâ poscere jus esset.

Accedebat aliud, si in navigando ex decreto confensuque vectorum jasturam aliquam mercium facere, ad confervandas cum nave & vectoribus res reliquas tempestatis exortæ jus cogeret, & si quid hostibus forte pendendum esset, tum ut liceret & jasturam illam, & quod hostibus expensum, in ratio-nes inferre, & summæ debiti detrahere.

Sed Demosthenem ipsum de his legibus differentem audiamus: Nostiu[?] professio, judices, (ait,) legem, quam ea severa sit, si quis Atheniensium alio quopiam quam Athenas flumentum vexerit, aut pecuniam mutuo dederit in alium mercatum, quam Atheniensium: quæ pœna de his sint constituta, quam magna, quam graves. Et his partem verborum legis subjicit: Argentum autem non liceat ulli Atheniensium, aut inquilinorum Athenis degentium, quorum hi sunt autores, (forte

page.notes: Reading uncertain: "Nostiu" (first word of the quotation) is marked [?]. The word "jasturam" is printed with a long s and is copied as "jasturam" (the printed form, possibly "jacturam"). "hæs" in the second paragraph is printed as such (probably "hæc") and is left as printed. The top of the page reads "176" and "DESCRIPTIO" in spaced capitals. The page ends mid-sentence with "(forte", and the continuation is on the next page.
